title: Elodie and the Summit
premise: Desert ranger Xanthe Crane has spent fifteen years chasing thieves across the salt flats, keeping her past buried deeper than any well. When an anomalous tide exposes a cave holding the wreck of the Meridian Star—a vessel that sank a century ago in what is now desert—she realizes the thief she's been tracking stole a map leading to it. Racing the salvage fleet and the dying season's last six tides, Xanthe must decide whether to reclaim her stolen identity as the wreck's true heir or stay invisible to protect the people who depend on her silence. She beats the fleet by one tide, claims the truth at terrible cost, and chooses love over duty by burning the salvage contract—keeping only the cave, and the life it lets her finally live.
about_author: Rosalind Eriksen is a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping coastlines that no longer exist. She writes adventure novels about landscapes that remember more than the people crossing them.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Tracking thief Casimir Voss across the flats, she reflects on fifteen years of measured distances and avoided names. When she finds his abandoned camp with half-burned charts of a coastline that shouldn't exist, curiosity overrides protocol. Emotional beat: restlessness—the first crack in her carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: The Tide That Lies
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. An impossible tide floods the dry basin, revealing a sea cave sealed for a century. Inside: the Meridian Star's hull, preserved in salt, and markings matching Voss's charts. Legends said the cave charged admission; now she understands the price is witness. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as she hears engines—salvage scouts on the horizon.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She calculates the dry season's end: six tides before the cave seals forever. The salvage fleet, led by iron-handed Broker Adhara Quill, will arrive in eight. Xanthe must move the evidence—or herself—first. Emotional beat: cold resolve masking fear as she sends a coded message to the one person from her old life.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Knew Her Name
chapters.summary: Dual POV begins. Xanthe corners Voss in a canyon waystation; he doesn't run—he waits, because he stole the map to lure her out. He knew her before she was Crane: she is the Meridian Star captain's granddaughter, presumed drowned with the ship's registry. Emotional beat: vertigo—her identity surfacing like the wreck itself.

chapters.title: What the Salt Keeps
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He explains the registry below names heirs to the wreck's cargo—and to debts the salvage fleet wants erased. He needed the heir alive to open the captain's strongbox. Xanthe refuses; loyalty to her ranger post demands she report the find, which means surrendering it. Emotional beat: the first true collision of duty and truth.

chapters.title: Adhara Quill Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The fleet jumps schedule—two tides early. Quill offers Xanthe a finder's fee to sign away all claims, revealing she knows exactly who Crane used to be. Signing means safety and erasure; refusing means war. Emotional beat: pressure tightening as love interest and deputy ranger Sef arrives, forcing her to choose what he'll learn.

chapters.title: Loyalty Weighs Less Than Water
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef discovers Xanthe's deception about the cave and confronts her—not with betrayal but with a choice: he'll stand with her if she tells him the whole truth. She does, all of it, including the name she buried. Emotional beat: intimacy forged through confession; love against duty made literal between two officers of the law.

chapters.title: The Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. With Sef and a reluctant Voss, she dives the flooding cave to reach the strongbox before Quill's divers. Voss takes a wound covering their escape; the registry surfaces with names that indict Quill's own house. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by cost—Voss bleeding out on the sand, the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Summit
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Climax at the cave mouth as the final tides rage. Quill's fleet closes in; Xanthe reads the registry aloud to the assembled crews, exposing the debts and murders the salvage contract was built to bury. The crews turn; Quill retreats rather than face mutiny. Emotional beat: blazing confrontation—truth wielded as a weapon, duty fulfilled by breaking the contract.

chapters.title: Admission Paid
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Resolution. The cave seals with the dry season, its secrets legally hers and practically unclaimable. Voss recovers and vanishes, forgiven. Xanthe takes back her birth name, keeps her post on her own terms, and stays—with Sef—in sight of the water that found her. Emotional beat: quiet arrival home after fifteen years of miles.
